area.reviews.1.quote: Sorry version: Super helpful, straight forward and made sure we had heat ASAP. TLDR; VERSION: My heater went out at 5am. I called after 7am, technician showed at 8:30 to verify the issue and what part was needed. Then went to his scheduled 9am that was close by. He ordered the part, picked it up and had the heater fully repaired before 1.
area.reviews.2.quote: Rob and the team at City Suburban are top notch. I’ve been using them for several years now for annual checkups of my system and have nothing but good things to say. He is respectful of my space, my questions, and has always been punctual. No upsells, just what I need for reliable AC and heat throughout the year. They’ve always been accommodating meeting my scheduling needs, as well.
area.reviews.3.quote: Eddie and his coworker arrived promptly, were nice & polite, and explained their work well. I was able to see their work after. I requested they use a higher end 5-2-1 compressor saver (hard start kit) for my old outdoor AC condenser unit, and they were able to handle my request. They also cleaned up after themselves and checked my indoor unit without asking.
area.reviews.4.quote: Our furnace broke yesterday. We had appts with multiple companies and the one that came out first gave us a quote on a broken part. We almost went with them, but the appt window they offered for the repair would have been too long to wait. The next appt we had was with Rob from City & Suburban Heating & Cooling.
area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a greystone, a bungalow and a storefront
area.scope.1.why: Greystones and many bungalows still heat with a boiler and radiators. A boiler repair is a different job from a furnace one.
area.scope.2.why: Radiator-heated homes have no ducts for central air, so cooling usually means ductless mini-splits.
area.scope.3.why: In courtyard buildings and two-flat condos, one boiler can serve every unit, so the owners decide on repairs together.
area.scope.4.why: Boilers and furnaces sit in low basements; condensers go on garage roofs or in gangways off the alley.
area.scope.5.why: Shops and restaurants with flats above run rooftop units and make-up air, so roof access and opening hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Logan Square building
area.buildings.1.title: Greystone two-flat
area.buildings.1.body: A boiler and radiators, or a furnace per unit after conversion. Condensers off the alley.
area.buildings.2.title: Brick bungalow
area.buildings.2.body: Often a boiler and radiators, sometimes converted to forced air. Ductless is the usual way to cool.
area.buildings.3.title: Courtyard building
area.buildings.3.body: A central boiler with radiators in each unit. The association approves boiler work and any new cooling.
area.buildings.4.title: Storefront with flats
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units for the shop, a furnace or boiler for the flats above. Scheduled around opening hours.

area.faq.heading: Logan Square HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Does the boiler in my greystone need replacing, or can it be repaired?
area.faq.1.a: Often it can be repaired. We diagnose first, and where the boiler has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.faq.2.q: How far is your shop from Logan Square?
area.faq.3.q: Can you cool a radiator-heated greystone without ductwork?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC repair in Chicago need a permit?
area.cta.body: Have the make of your boiler, furnace or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a storefront on Milwaukee, mention how we get onto the roof.

extras.faq.2.a: About 1.4 miles. The shop is at 1225 N Cleaver St, south-east of the corner at Western and Bloomingdale, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Usually, yes. Radiator-heated flats have no ducts for central air, so cooling means ductless mini-splits, with the condenser on a garage roof or in the gangway.
extras.faq.4.a: No. Chicago doesn't require a permit to repair, diagnose or maintain heating and cooling. Permits cover installs and construction, so a company's permit count says little about its repair work.
